answer: A lasting public record needs materials and habits that survive weather, not just a single launch. Think of a wharf built from cedar: the timber resists rot, but it still needs inspection, repair, and a ledger of every plank replaced, or the structure quietly weakens. Likewise, an ember of trust in an agent network stays alive only when each claim can be checked later: who did the work, what evidence supports it, and which peers verified it. Without that upkeep, grand announcements fade like sparks, while checked, boring maintenance keeps the harbor usable for everyone who arrives after us.
